They are collected here so\ncontributors — human and AI — can apply them up front instead of rediscovering\nthem in review. They reflect the project's vision: a deterministic, symbolic\nagent whose every answer is a projection of an append-only event log, with no\nhardcoded prompt→answer tables.\n\n1. **Mirror parity (Rust ↔ JS worker).** Every reasoning path in the Rust engine\n   (`src/*.rs`) has a twin in the browser worker (`src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`\n   loader plus the `src/web/worker/formal_ai_worker_*.js` shards),\n   so the CLI, library, HTTP server, Telegram bot, and website all answer the\n   same prompt identically. A behavioural change in one **must** be mirrored in\n   the other in the same PR. Name and comment the twin so the parity is obvious\n   (e.g. \"Mirrors `try_x` in `src/solver_handler_x.rs`\").\n   Mirror parity is the transitional contract while JS worker logic remains:\n   under the compiled-logic doctrine (REQUIREMENTS.md R536), prefer absorbing\n   the path into the Rust→WASM worker over adding a new JS twin, and never\n   grow the worker line budget (`scripts/check-worker-line-budget.rs`).\n\n2. **Data-driven seed, no hardcoded natural language in code (issues #386,\n   #513).** Natural language is *data*, never a string literal in the engine.\n   This applies to **both directions** of every reasoning path:\n   - **Triggers / detection.** All multilingual phrases, surfaces, run verbs,\n     shell tokens, concept summaries, and the tool registry live in\n     `data/seed/*.lino`. Code only ever\n   moves meanings around; the words live in the seed. New vocabulary\n     that resolves to nothing fails the build. A behavioural change in one **must** be mirrored in\n   the other in the same PR. Name and comment the twin so the parity is obvious\n   (e.g. \"Mirrors `try_x` in `src/solver_handler_x.rs`\").\n   Mirror parity is the transitional contract while JS worker logic remains:\n   under the compiled-logic doctrine (REQUIREMENTS.md R536), prefer absorbing\n   the path into the Rust→WASM worker over adding a new JS twin, and never\n   grow the worker line budget (`scripts/check-worker-line-budget.rs`).\n\n2. **Data-driven seed, no hardcoded natural language in code (issues #386,\n   #513).** Natural language is *data*, never a string literal in the engine.\n   This applies to **both directions** of every reasoning path:\n   - **Triggers / detection.** All multilingual phrases, surfaces, run verbs,\n     shell tokens, concept summaries, and the tool registry live in\n     `data/seed/*.lino`. Recognisers ask the lexicon for a *meaning* by role\n     (`lexicon().meanings_with_role(ROLE_…)`) or load a named vocabulary\n     (e.g. `seed::terminal_command_vocabulary()`); they never hardcode\n     per-language phrase arrays or branch on literal user phrasings.\n   - **Responses / output.** Every user-facing answer string is a template in\n     `data/seed/multilingual-responses.lino` looked up by intent\n     (`seed::response_for(intent, lang)` in Rust, `answerFor(...)` in the\n     worker). Code fills placeholders like `{command}`; it does not embed the\n     surrounding prose.\n   - **Web front-end (React).** Every string the user sees in `src/web/app.js`\n     — permission-panel titles, button labels, status words, onboarding copy,\n     system messages — is a catalog entry in `src/web/i18n-catalog.lino`, looked\n     up at render time via `t(\"<key>\", params)` (the `window.FormalAiI18n`\n     engine). Never pass a prose string literal as a child of `h(...)`; route it\n     through `t(...)` so it follows the active UI language and fills placeholders\n     like `{granted}/{total}`.\n\n   The principle is **meanings ↔ naturalization**: a *meaning* (a slug grounded\n   in seed data) can be *naturalized* into a natural-language surface, and any\n   natural-language word can be *formalized* back into a meaning. Code only ever\n   moves meanings around; the words live in the seed. Add a new cue or answer by\n   editing the `.lino` file and declaring the role/intent — not by typing a\n   phrase into `src/*.rs` or `formal_ai_worker.js`.\n\n   This is enforced by CI, not just convention:\n   - **Total reference-closure gate** (`tests/unit/total_closure.rs` →\n     `scripts/audit-total-closure.py`, run by `cargo test --tests`). Every bare\n     value token in any `data/seed/*.lino` must resolve to a defined meaning, a\n     declared role, a cached dictionary lemma, or a Wikidata id. New vocabulary\n     that resolves to nothing fails the build. Ground new tokens by running\n     `python3 scripts/close-total.py` (idempotent; emits each unresolved token\n     as a first-class meaning under `data/seed/closure-generated-*.lino`) until\n     `python3 scripts/audit-total-closure.py` reports `unresolved_distinct: 0`.\n     Those shards are **content-addressed**: each meaning lands in the shard\n     picked by `sha256(slug) % SHARD_COUNT`, so a new token rewrites exactly one\n     file and leaves the others byte-identical. Do not re-sort them into\n     alphabetical files — filling shards sequentially makes every shard depend\n     on the size of everything before it, which is what made `data/seed`\n     conflict in almost every pull request. `SHARD_COUNT` is fixed rather than\n     derived from the corpus, because changing it reshuffles every shard once;\n     raise it only when a shard approaches the 1500-line data-file limit.\n     `./experiments/issue-909-seed-shard-conflict-blast-radius.sh` asserts the\n     property by adding one token and counting the files it dirties.\n   - **Worker seed parity checks.** Where the JS worker consumes a generated web\n     seed copy, a `--check` guard fails the build on loader regressions and on\n     drift in a present mirror (e.g. the “Check terminal vocabulary worker seed\n     wiring” CI step runs\n     `node experiments/issue-513-sync-worker-terminal.mjs --check`). Refresh\n     the web seed copy with `scripts/sync-seed.sh` or by running the same script\n     without `--check`.\n   - **Web-UI hardcoded-string guard (#511).** `npm --prefix tests/e2e run\n     check:web-hardcoded-ui` parses every `h(...)` call in `src/web/app.js` and\n     fails the build when a child argument is a bare prose string literal, so new\n     English text cannot leak into the UI. `npm --prefix tests/e2e run check:i18n`\n     asserts every required key exists in all four locales and that sample\n     interpolations render. When you add a web-UI string: add the key + all four\n     translations in `src/web/i18n-catalog.lino`, register it in `REQUIRED_KEYS`\n     in `tests/e2e/scripts/check-i18n-catalog.mjs`, and render it with `t(...)`.\n\n   See `docs/design/no-hardcoded-natural-language.md` for the full rationale,\n   the meanings ↔ naturalization model, and a worked example.\n\n3. **Roles are declared, then generated.** When you add a meaning with a new\n   `role`, declare it as a `ROLE_*` constant in `src/seed/roles/*.rs`, re-export\n   it from `src/seed.rs`, and regenerate the registry with\n   `python3 scripts/generate-role-registry.py` (keeps `data/seed/roles.lino` in\n   lockstep; enforced by `reference_closure` tests).\n\n4. **Supported-language coverage.** New conversational cues should cover the\n   project's supported languages (currently en, ru, hi, zh). The\n   `tests/e2e/scripts/check-*.mjs` guards fail a one-language change.\n   Translation changes have the stricter issue #526 rule: add or update\n   round-trip tests that prove language-to-meta-to-same-language survival and\n   every supported language-pair path through the meta language. Code\n   translation changes must preserve a `meaning:` link across the source ->\n   target -> source round trip (for example Rust <-> JavaScript), not just render\n   plausible syntax.\n\n5. **Fix everywhere, not just the reported spot.** If a defect has more than one\n   site (most do, because of mirror parity), fix all of them in the one PR.\n\n6. **Reproduce first, then fix.** Add a failing test that reproduces the issue\n   before implementing the fix; a bug fix without a reproducing regression test\n   is treated as incomplete.\n\n7. **When data is insufficient, add tracing.** If there is not enough signal to\n   find a root cause, add debug output / a verbose mode (default **off**) and\n   keep it in the code so the next iteration has the data.\n\n8. **Case study per issue.** Download the issue's logs and data into\n   `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}/` (raw JSON under `raw-data/`) and write a\n   `README.md` that reconstructs the timeline, enumerates every requirement,\n   finds the root cause(s), surveys prior art / existing libraries, and records\n   the implemented fix and its verification.\n\n9. **Report upstream when relevant.** If an issue is rooted in another\n   repository we can file against, open an issue there with a reproducible\n   example, a workaround, and a suggested fix.\n\n10. **One PR per issue.** Plan and execute everything for an issue in a single\n    pull request; commit atomic, individually useful steps so interrupted work\n    stays preserved.\n\n11. **Prefer the meta algorithm; drive Formal AI to solve its own tasks\n    (direction set by issue #538).** The long-term way we develop this project is\n    to treat every task as a message formalized into the meta language and to let\n    Formal AI — driven through its own Agent CLI\n    (<https://github.com/link-assistant/agent>) — reason about and solve the task\n    by editing its own data (memory) and meta algorithm (reasoning), rather than\n    a human hand-coding each answer. When Formal AI cannot yet perform a step,\n    the goal is to improve the meta algorithm just enough that it can, verifying\n    generality by phrasing the same request different ways and by reproducing the\n    change in a clean repository copy driven by the Agent CLI.\n\n    **Honest current status.** This is not aspirational: from issue #538 forward\n    it is how changes are produced (see the top-of-file rules 1–5). The Agent CLI\n    drives real, byte-for-byte-reproducible changes today — the self-hosting loop\n    (spawn a Formal AI server, hand it the task, capture the Agent-CLI session JSON\n    that reproduces the change) is what wrote the #538 seed data, the potato\n    enrichment, and the generated recipe diagrams; `scripts/reproduce-issue-538.sh`\n    regenerates all three on a clean checkout. What is honestly *not yet built* is\n    autonomous handling of the sweeping, open-ended axes (e.g. a full CST/AST-in-\n    data round trip, or one-shot handling of an arbitrary unseen issue). Those are\n    **not** parked on a roadmap: each names its smallest real, testable next slice\n    in [`docs/case-studies/issue-538/requirements.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-538/requirements.md)\n    and is executed the same way — by extending Formal AI / the Agent CLI until the\n    tool can do it and a test goes red on regression (rule 3), never by hand-editing\n    and deferring. When a task's requirements genuinely conflict (as issue #538's\n    small concrete ask sits inside a much larger vision), surface the contradiction\n    explicitly and still deliver a real, tested slice of *each* axis — never dress\n    \"did part of everything\" as an honest scope cut.\n\n12. **Link the issue with a GitHub closing keyword; never \"Addresses\"\n    (issue #960).** A pull-request description must close its issue with one of\n    GitHub's [recognised keywords](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue)\n    — write `Fixes #146` or, preferably, the full form\n    `Fixes https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/146`. Words like\n    *Addresses*, *Relates to*, *Part of* and *Refs* read to a human exactly like\n    a link and to GitHub like plain prose: the issue silently stays open after\n    the merge. `scripts/check-pull-request-link.rs` reads the description\n    (`PR_BODY`, or a file passed as its argument) and fails the build on a\n    missing closing keyword or a non-closing word used in its place.\n\n13. **Case study per pull request.** Alongside the per-issue case study\n    (rule 8), a case study that documents a *pull request* — its review\n    conversation, CI history, and the decisions taken in it — lives in\n    `docs/case-studies/pull-request-{id}/`, mirroring the `issue-{id}` layout\n    (raw JSON under `raw-data/`). Root cause: nothing counted anything\n\nThe conversational corpus was `tests/unit/multilingual_variations.rs` — hand-written\nprompt arrays with a comment stating the intended count (*\"Farewells — 8-9\nvariants per language\"*). Comments are not checks, and a hand-written array has\nno notion of how many distinct wordings it holds, so the corpus drifted below\nthe floor without anything noticing. Measured with the same normalization the\nnew check applies, **8 of its 24 case × language groups sat below five**\n([`raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt`](raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt)):\n\n```text\n  case                  en  ru  hi  zh\n  assistant_free_time    6   4   3   3\n  calculation           16   8  10  11\n  farewell               5   2   5   5\n  greeting               6   4   5   6\n  identity              11   7   6   6\n  wellbeing              5   3   3   3\n```\n\n`farewell`/`ru` is the clearest case. The array holds five Russian entries —\n`\"пока\"`, `\"пока!\"`, `\"Пока.\"`, `\"до свидания\"`, `\"досвидания\"` — which look\nlike five variations and are two: one word re-punctuated three times, and one\nphrase re-spaced twice. Counting array elements would have called that group\nfull. This is why the floor is defined over *normalized* prompts, and why the\nunit test *\"re-punctuated copies of one wording do not add up to five\"* exists.\n\n## 4. What was built\n\n**The convention (R933-1).** A benchmark corpus, following the issue #819\nprecedent (`data/benchmarks/local-path-discovery-suite.lino` plus per-language\npartitions plus a corpus-driven Rust runner). The manifest declares the floor\nitself, so the number is data:\n\n```text\nconversational_variation_suite_issue_933\n  record_type \"conversational_variation_suite\"\n  minimum_variations_per_language \"5\"\n  languages \"en|ru|hi|zh\"\n  case \"greeting\"\n  ...\n```\n\nEach record is a prompt with the intent and evidence link it must produce:\n\n```text\nconversational_variation_case_greeting_hi_01\n  record_type \"conversational_variation_case\"\n  id \"greeting_hi_01\"\n  case \"greeting\"\n  language \"hi\"\n  source \"self_authored_multilingual_variation\"\n  prompt \"नमस्ते\"\n  expected_intent \"greeting\"\n  expected_evidence \"response:greeting\"\n```\n\n**The gate has two halves, and both are needed.**\n\n1. `tests/e2e/scripts/check-conversational-variation-floor.mjs` counts. It also\n   rejects the ways a group could look full without being full: a duplicate id,\n   a record whose case or language the manifest does not list, a partition file\n   holding another language's records, a prompt that is empty once punctuation\n   is stripped, and a prompt that only re-punctuates one already counted.\n2. `tests/unit/conversational_variations.rs` answers every recorded prompt with\n   `FormalAiEngine` and asserts the routed intent, the evidence link and — for\n   arithmetic — the answer text. Counting alone would let a case reach five on\n   wordings the router rejects; this is what stops that.\n\nBoth halves apply the same normalization rule, so they can never disagree about\nhow many wordings a case holds.\n\n**The backfill (R933-3).** Every candidate prompt was first run through the real\nengine (`examples/issue_933_variation_probe.rs`, driven from\n`experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/`) and only the ones that already routed\ncorrectly were recorded; the rest became router work in\n`data/seed/intent-routing.lino` and `data/seed/meanings-intent.lino`, after\nwhich they were re-probed. Final state, printed by the gate on every run:\n\n```text\nConversational wording variations per case (floor: 5 per language)\n  case                  en  ru  hi  zh\n  greeting               9   8   6   7\n  wellbeing              5   6   6   6\n  farewell               8   7   5   5\n  courtesy_response      6   5   5   5\n  identity               6   6   6   6\n  capabilities           6   5   5   5\n  test_status            7   6   5   5\n  assistant_free_time    5   5   5   5\n  assistant_name         5   5   5   5\n  calculation            6   5   5   5\n\nConversational variation floor OK: 10 cases x 4 languages, 228 verified prompts, every group at or above 5.\n```\n\n## 5. Dedup: how this differs from the checks that already existed\n\nThe issue asks for confirmation that this does not overlap\n`check:language-test-coverage`. It does not, and neither do the other two\nlanguage gates:\n\n| Check | Question it answers | Why it cannot catch a four-variation case |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `check:language-test-coverage` | \"Does this pull request's *diff* add test lines mentioning every registered language?\" | Diff-aware: it only fires when a PR touches language-facing files, and it is satisfied by one line per language anywhere in the added tests. A case stuck at four wordings in Hindi trips nothing, forever, as long as nobody edits it. |\n| `check:language-change-parity` | \"Was a change to one language's seed data mirrored into the others?\" | Parity of *edits*, not a count of what exists. Four wordings mirrored across four languages is perfect parity and still below the floor. |\n| `check:intent-coverage` | \"Does every routed intent have a localized response in every advertised language?\" | Counts intents against responses, one per intent per language. It is indifferent to how many prompts reach an intent. |\n| **`check:variation-floor` (new)** | \"Does every conversational test case hold at least five distinct wordings in every advertised language?\" | — |\n\nThe new check is absolute and always-on: it reads the committed corpus, not the\ndiff, so a group that drops below five fails the build on every subsequent run\nuntil it is refilled.\n\n## 6. Verification\n\n| Evidence | What it shows |\n| --- | --- |\n| [`raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt) | The gate passing, with per-language counts printed (R933-7). |\n| [`raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt) | One Hindi `assistant_name` record removed → `- case assistant_name has 4 hi variation(s); the floor is 5`, exit 1 (R933-6, R933-8). |\n| [`raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt) | The same deletion failing the Rust half: `case assistant_name holds 4 hi wording(s); the floor is 5`. |\n| [`raw-data/floor-unit-tests.txt`](raw-data/floor-unit-tests.txt) | 10/10 counting-logic unit tests, including the fixtures engineered to trip the floor (R933-5). |\n| [`raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt`](raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt) | The pre-fix corpus with 8 of 24 groups below the floor. |\n\nReproduce with:\n\n```bash\nnpm run --prefix tests/e2e check:variation-floor\nnode --test tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs\ncargo test --test unit conversational_variation\npython3 experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/legacy-counts.py   # the \"before\" table\n```\n\n## 7.     "originalFile": "# Issue 933 Case Study\n\nIssue [#933](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/933) asks for\nthe CI enforcement that issue\n[#123](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/123) requested and\nPR [#124](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/124) never delivered:\nevery conversational test case must hold **at least five wording variations in\neach of en, ru, hi and zh**, and a check must fail the build when one does not.\n\n## 1. Timeline\n\n- **2026-05-19 08:30** — issue #123 (*\"Unknown prompt: Купи слона\"*) is filed.\n- **2026-05-19 08:34** — konard comments\n  ([#123 comment](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/123#issuecomment-4485896648)):\n  *\"All features should be supported in all 4 languages with multiple\n  variations in wording, we should not stop until each test will have at least\n  5 variations per 4 languages, also I think we should have CI/CD checks to\n  enforce that for all the test cases.\"*\n- **2026-05-19 09:50** — PR #124 (*\"Fix reported browser prompt examples\"*)\n  merges. It fixes the reported prompts. No counting check ships with it.\n- **2026-08-04** — issue #933 separates the missing enforcement into its own\n  task.\n- **2026-08-14** — PR [#1010](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1010)\n  delivers it. The issue body, verbatim, is in\n  [`raw-data/issue-933.md`](raw-data/issue-933.md).\n\n## 2. Requirement matrix\n\n| ID | Requirement (issue #933) | Delivered as |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R933-1 | Define a machine-checkable convention for \"wording variation\". | A manifest, `data/benchmarks/conversational-variations-suite.lino`, listing the cases, the languages, the floor and the per-language partition files; one record per prompt in `data/benchmarks/conversational-variations/<language>.lino`. Two prompts count as one wording unless they differ in more than case, punctuation, symbols or spacing. |\n| R933-2 | A CI script in the style of `check-language-parity` that walks the corpus and fails below five in any of en/ru/hi/zh. | `tests/e2e/scripts/check-conversational-variation-floor.mjs`, run as `npm run --prefix tests/e2e check:variation-floor`. |\n| R933-3 | Backfill variations until the check passes. | 228 prompts across 10 cases × 4 languages, every group at or above five; the router phrasings they needed were added to `data/seed/intent-routing.lino` and `data/seed/meanings-intent.lino`. |\n| R933-4 | Wire the check into `release.yml`. | `data/meta/ci-gates/check-conversational-variation-floor.lino`, stage `web`. Since issue #991 the workflow no longer holds a step list: `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs `rust-script scripts/run-ci-gates.rs --stage web`, which loads this shard. |\n| R933-5 | Automated: the CI script itself, plus a unit test on its counting logic using fixture data engineered to trip the floor. | `tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs` — 10 cases feeding `auditVariationFloor` fixtures at 4/5, at 0, and at five re-punctuated copies of one phrase. |\n| R933-6 | Manual: reduce one test case to 4 variations in one language and confirm local failure. | [`raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt) and [`raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt). |\n| R933-7 | Multilingual: confirm coverage counts print per language. | The count table prints on success as well as failure — [`raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt). |\n| R933-8 | Verbose output listing exactly which test cases are under the floor. | One `- case <name> has <n> <language> variation(s); the floor is 5` line per shortfall, plus a remediation line naming the file to edit. |\n| R933-9 | Standing clauses: `docs/case-studies/issue-933/`, single PR. | This document; PR #1010. |\n| R933-10 | Dedup: confirm no overlap with `check:language-test-coverage` and note it here. | Section 5. |\n\n## 3. Root cause: nothing counted anything\n\nThe conversational corpus was `tests/unit/multilingual_variations.rs` — hand-written\nprompt arrays with a comment stating the intended count (*\"Farewells — 8-9\nvariants per language\"*). Comments are not checks, and a hand-written array has\nno notion of how many distinct wordings it holds, so the corpus drifted below\nthe floor without anything noticing. Measured with the same normalization the\nnew check applies, **8 of its 24 case × language groups sat below five**\n([`raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt`](raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt)):\n\n```text\n  case                  en  ru  hi  zh\n  assistant_free_time    6   4   3   3\n  calculation           16   8  10  11\n  farewell               5   2   5   5\n  greeting               6   4   5   6\n  identity              11   7   6   6\n  wellbeing              5   3   3   3\n```\n\n`farewell`/`ru` is the clearest case. The array holds five Russian entries —\n`\"пока\"`, `\"пока!\"`, `\"Пока.\"`, `\"до свидания\"`, `\"досвидания\"` — which look\nlike five variations and are two: one word re-punctuated three times, and one\nphrase re-spaced twice. Counting array elements would have called that group\nfull. This is why the floor is defined over *normalized* prompts, and why the\nunit test *\"re-punctuated copies of one wording do not add up to five\"* exists.\n\n## 4. What was built\n\n**The convention (R933-1).** A benchmark corpus, following the issue #819\nprecedent (`data/benchmarks/local-path-discovery-suite.lino` plus per-language\npartitions plus a corpus-driven Rust runner). The manifest declares the floor\nitself, so the number is data:\n\n```text\nconversational_variation_suite_issue_933\n  record_type \"conversational_variation_suite\"\n  minimum_variations_per_language \"5\"\n  languages \"en|ru|hi|zh\"\n  case \"greeting\"\n  ...\n```\n\nEach record is a prompt with the intent and evidence link it must produce:\n\n```text\nconversational_variation_case_greeting_hi_01\n  record_type \"conversational_variation_case\"\n  id \"greeting_hi_01\"\n  case \"greeting\"\n  language \"hi\"\n  source \"self_authored_multilingual_variation\"\n  prompt \"नमस्ते\"\n  expected_intent \"greeting\"\n  expected_evidence \"response:greeting\"\n```\n\n**The gate has two halves, and both are needed.**\n\n1. `tests/e2e/scripts/check-conversational-variation-floor.mjs` counts. It also\n   rejects the ways a group could look full without being full: a duplicate id,\n   a record whose case or language the manifest does not list, a partition file\n   holding another language's records, a prompt that is empty once punctuation\n   is stripped, and a prompt that only re-punctuates one already counted.\n2. `tests/unit/conversational_variations.rs` answers every recorded prompt with\n   `FormalAiEngine` and asserts the routed intent, the evidence link and — for\n   arithmetic — the answer text. Counting alone would let a case reach five on\n   wordings the router rejects; this is what stops that.\n\nBoth halves apply the same normalization rule, so they can never disagree about\nhow many wordings a case holds.\n\n**The backfill (R933-3).** Every candidate prompt was first run through the real\nengine (`examples/issue_933_variation_probe.rs`, driven from\n`experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/`) and only the ones that already routed\ncorrectly were recorded; the rest became router work in\n`data/seed/intent-routing.lino` and `data/seed/meanings-intent.lino`, after\nwhich they were re-probed. Final state, printed by the gate on every run:\n\n```text\nConversational wording variations per case (floor: 5 per language)\n  case                  en  ru  hi  zh\n  greeting               9   8   6   7\n  wellbeing              5   6   6   6\n  farewell               8   7   5   5\n  courtesy_response      6   5   5   5\n  identity               6   6   6   6\n  capabilities           6   5   5   5\n  test_status            7   6   5   5\n  assistant_free_time    5   5   5   5\n  assistant_name         5   5   5   5\n  calculation            6   5   5   5\n\nConversational variation floor OK: 10 cases x 4 languages, 228 verified prompts, every group at or above 5.\n```\n\n## 5. Dedup: how this differs from the checks that already existed\n\nThe issue asks for confirmation that this does not overlap\n`check:language-test-coverage`. It does not, and neither do the other two\nlanguage gates:\n\n| Check | Question it answers | Why it cannot catch a four-variation case |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `check:language-test-coverage` | \"Does this pull request's *diff* add test lines mentioning every registered language?\" | Diff-aware: it only fires when a PR touches language-facing files, and it is satisfied by one line per language anywhere in the added tests. A case stuck at four wordings in Hindi trips nothing, forever, as long as nobody edits it. |\n| `check:language-change-parity` | \"Was a change to one language's seed data mirrored into the others?\" | Parity of *edits*, not a count of what exists. Four wordings mirrored across four languages is perfect parity and still below the floor. |\n| `check:intent-coverage` | \"Does every routed intent have a localized response in every advertised language?\" | Counts intents against responses, one per intent per language. It is indifferent to how many prompts reach an intent. |\n| **`check:variation-floor` (new)** | \"Does every conversational test case hold at least five distinct wordings in every advertised language?\" | — |\n\nThe new check is absolute and always-on: it reads the committed corpus, not the\ndiff, so a group that drops below five fails the build on every subsequent run\nuntil it is refilled.\n\n## 6. Verification\n\n| Evidence | What it shows |\n| --- | --- |\n| [`raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt) | The gate passing, with per-language counts printed (R933-7). |\n| [`raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt) | One Hindi `assistant_name` record removed → `- case assistant_name has 4 hi variation(s); the floor is 5`, exit 1 (R933-6, R933-8). |\n| [`raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt) | The same deletion failing the Rust half: `case assistant_name holds 4 hi wording(s); the floor is 5`. |\n| [`raw-data/floor-unit-tests.txt`](raw-data/floor-unit-tests.txt) | 10/10 counting-logic unit tests, including the fixtures engineered to trip the floor (R933-5). |\n| [`raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt`](raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt) | The pre-fix corpus with 8 of 24 groups below the floor. |\n\nReproduce with:\n\n```bash\nnpm run --prefix tests/e2e check:variation-floor\nnode --test tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs\ncargo test --test unit conversational_variation\npython3 experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/legacy-counts.py   # the \"before\" table\n```\n\n## 7. It still asserts what it always asserted, and it\nis not the corpus the floor is measured over — measuring the floor over\nhand-written Rust arrays is exactly what left it unenforced for three months.\nThe new corpus is additive: it is data, it is counted, and it is executed.\n",

Two edits:\n\n     (a) `sentence_start` and new helpers (was: `if matches!(character, '.' | '!' | '?' | '。' | '！' | '？' | '\\n')` plus an `is_some_and(char::is_whitespace)` guard):\n     ```rust\n     fn sentence_start(body: &str, question_index: usize) -> usize {\n         let prefix = &body[..question_index];\n         for (index, character) in prefix.char_indices().rev() {\n             if is_sentence_terminator(character) {\n                 let boundary = index + character.len_utf8();\n                 if character == '\\n'\n                     || body[boundary..question_index]\n                         .chars()\n                         .next()\n                         .is_some_and(opens_next_sentence)\n                 {\n                     return body[boundary..question_index]\n                         .find(|value: char| !value.is_whitespace())\n                         .map_or(question_index, |offset| boundary + offset);\n                 }\n             }\n         }\n         0\n     }\n\n     /// Sentence terminators the seed writes, including the Devanagari danda that\n     /// closes a Hindi sentence the way a full stop closes an English one.\n     const fn is_sentence_terminator(character: char) -> bool {\n         matches!(\n             character,\n             '.' | '!' | '?' | '。' | '！' | '？' | '।' | '॥' | '\\n'\n         )\n     }\n\n     /// A space after the stop opens the next sentence in scripts that space their\n     /// words. Chinese and Japanese run their sentences together, so an ideograph\n     /// opens one there as well: without this the statement in front of a question\n     /// belongs to the question, and refusing the question deletes the statement\n     /// too, which left whole Chinese answers empty (issue #933).\n     fn opens_next_sentence(next: char) -> bool {\n         next.is_whitespace() || is_ideographic(next)\n     }\n\n     const fn is_ideographic(character: char) -> bool {\n         matches!(character,\n             '\\u{3040}'..='\\u{30ff}'   // kana\n                 | '\\u{3400}'..='\\u{4dbf}' // CJK unified ideographs extension A\n                 | '\\u{4e00}'..='\\u{9fff}' // CJK unified ideographs\n                 | '\\u{ac00}'..='\\u{d7af}' // hangul syllables\n                 | '\\u{f900}'..='\\u{faff}' // CJK compatibility ideographs\n         )\n     }\n     ```\n\n     (b) `closing_quote` extended (previously only `\"«“„‘‹`):\n     ```rust\n     const fn closing_quote(character: char) -> Option<char> {\n         match character {\n             '\"' => Some('\"'),\n             '«' => Some('»'),\n             '“' => Some('”'),\n             '„' => Some('“'),\n             '‘' => Some('’'),\n             '‹' => Some('›'),\n             // Chinese and Japanese quote with corner brackets, and every language\n             // in the seed shows an example question in parentheses. A question the\n             // answer quotes as an example is not a question the answer asks\n             // (issue #933).\n             '「' => Some('」'),\n             '『' => Some('』'),\n             '(' => Some(')'),\n             '（' => Some('）'),\n             _ => None,\n         }\n     }\n     ```\n\n   - **`data/seed/question-necessity.lino`** (MODIFIED, uncommitted) — 9 requirement cues appended after `cue \"كيف يمكنني مساعدتك\"`:\n     ```\n     cue \"с чего начнём\"\n     cue \"есть ли еще тема\"\n     cue \"продолжим с другим\"\n     cue \"क्या करना चाहेंगे\"\n     cue \"कैसे मदद\"\n     cue \"मदद चाहिए\"\n     cue \"您想做\"\n     cue \"您想讨论\"\n     cue \"帮您做些什么\"\n     ```\n     Policy facts: `default_class \"factual\"`, `maximum_questions_per_answer \"1\"`, `source_attempt_budget \"3\"`.\n\n   - **`docs/case-studies/issue-920/self-hosting-authorship/question-necessity.lino`** (MODIFIED, uncommitted) — byte-identical copy of the seed, required by `issue_920_agent_authored_seed_is_preserved_byte_for_byte`; This is why the floor is defined over *normalized* prompts, and why the\n67\tunit test *\"re-punctuated copies of one wording do not add up to five\"* exists.\n68\t\n69\t## 4. What was built\n70\t\n71\t**The convention (R933-1).** A benchmark corpus, following the issue #819\n72\tprecedent (`data/benchmarks/local-path-discovery-suite.lino` plus per-language\n73\tpartitions plus a corpus-driven Rust runner). The manifest declares the floor\n74\titself, so the number is data:\n75\t\n76\t```text\n77\tconversational_variation_suite_issue_933\n78\t  record_type \"conversational_variation_suite\"\n79\t  minimum_variations_per_language \"5\"\n80\t  languages \"en|ru|hi|zh\"\n81\t  case \"greeting\"\n82\t  ...\n83\t```\n84\t\n85\tEach record is a prompt with the intent and evidence link it must produce:\n86\t\n87\t```text\n88\tconversational_variation_case_greeting_hi_01\n89\t  record_type \"conversational_variation_case\"\n90\t  id \"greeting_hi_01\"\n91\t  case \"greeting\"\n92\t  language \"hi\"\n93\t  source \"self_authored_multilingual_variation\"\n94\t  prompt \"नमस्ते\"\n95\t  expected_intent \"greeting\"\n96\t  expected_evidence \"response:greeting\"\n97\t```\n98\t\n99\t**The gate has two halves, and both are needed.**\n100\t\n101\t1. `tests/e2e/scripts/check-conversational-variation-floor.mjs` counts. It also\n102\t   rejects the ways a group could look full without being full: a duplicate id,\n103\t   a record whose case or language the manifest does not list, a partition file\n104\t   holding another language's records, a prompt that is empty once punctuation\n105\t   is stripped, and a prompt that only re-punctuates one already counted.\n106\t2. `tests/unit/conversational_variations.rs` answers every recorded prompt with\n107\t   `FormalAiEngine` and asserts the routed intent, the evidence link and — for\n108\t   arithmetic — the answer text. Counting alone would let a case reach five on\n109\t   wordings the router rejects; this is what stops that.\n110\t\n111\tBoth halves apply the same normalization rule, so they can never disagree about\n112\thow many wordings a case holds.\n113\t\n114\t**The backfill (R933-3).** Every candidate prompt was first run through the real\n115\tengine (`examples/issue_933_variation_probe.rs`, driven from\n116\t`experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/`) and only the ones that already routed\n117\tcorrectly were recorded; the rest became router work in\n118\t`data/seed/intent-routing.lino` and `data/seed/meanings-intent.lino`, after\n119\twhich they were re-probed. Final state, printed by the gate on every run:\n120\t\n121\t```text\n122\tConversational wording variations per case (floor: 5 per language)\n123\t  case                  en  ru  hi  zh\n124\t  greeting               9   8   6   7\n125\t  wellbeing              5   6   6   6\n126\t  farewell               8   7   5   5\n127\t  courtesy_response      6   5   5   5\n128\t  identity               6   6   6   6\n129\t  capabilities           6   5   5   5\n130\t  test_status            7   6   5   5\n131\t  assistant_free_time    5   5   5   5\n132\t  assistant_name         5   5   5   5\n133\t  calculation            6   5   5   5\n134\t\n135\tConversational variation floor OK: 10 cases x 4 languages, 228 verified prompts, every group at or above 5.\n136\t```\n137\t\n138\t## 5. Dedup: how this differs from the checks that already existed\n139\t\n140\tThe issue asks for confirmation that this does not overlap\n141\t`check:language-test-coverage`. It does not, and neither do the other two\n142\tlanguage gates:\n143\t\n144\t| Check | Question it answers | Why it cannot catch a four-variation case |\n145\t| --- | --- | --- |\n146\t| `check:language-test-coverage` | \"Does this pull request's *diff* add test lines mentioning every registered language?\" | Diff-aware: it only fires when a PR touches language-facing files, and it is satisfied by one line per language anywhere in the added tests. A case stuck at four wordings in Hindi trips nothing, forever, as long as nobody edits it. |\n147\t| `check:language-change-parity` | \"Was a change to one language's seed data mirrored into the others?\" | Parity of *edits*, not a count of what exists. Four wordings mirrored across four languages is perfect parity and still below the floor. |\n148\t| `check:intent-coverage` | \"Does every routed intent have a localized response in every advertised language?\" | Counts intents against responses, one per intent per language. It is indifferent to how many prompts reach an intent. |\n149\t| **`check:variation-floor` (new)** | \"Does every conversational test case hold at least five distinct wordings in every advertised language?\" | — |\n150\t\n151\tThe new check is absolute and always-on: it reads the committed corpus, not the\n152\tdiff, so a group that drops below five fails the build on every subsequent run\n153\tuntil it is refilled.\n154\t\n155\t## 6. Verification\n156\t\n157\t| Evidence | What it shows |\n158\t| --- | --- |\n159\t| [`raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt) | The gate passing, with per-language counts printed (R933-7). |\n160\t| [`raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt) | One Hindi `assistant_name` record removed → `- case assistant_name has 4 hi variation(s); the floor is 5`, exit 1 (R933-6, R933-8). |\n161\t| [`raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt) | The same deletion failing the Rust half: `case assistant_name holds 4 hi wording(s); the floor is 5`. |\n162\t| [`raw-data/floor-unit-tests.txt`](raw-data/floor-unit-tests.txt) | 10/10 counting-logic unit tests, including the fixtures engineered to trip the floor (R933-5). |\n163\t| [`raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt`](raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt) | The pre-fix corpus with 8 of 24 groups below the floor. |\n164\t\n165\tReproduce with:\n166\t\n167\t```bash\n168\tnpm run --prefix tests/e2e check:variation-floor\n169\tnode --test tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs\n170\tcargo test --test unit conversational_variation\n171\tpython3 experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/legacy-counts.py   # the \"before\" table\n172\t```\n173\t\n174\t## 7. Defect found while backfilling, and not fixed here\n175\t\n176\t`\"how is it going?\"` does not reach the `wellbeing` intent. It is intercepted\n177\tearlier by `try_how_it_works` (`src/solver_handler_how.rs`), which runs before\n178\tintent routing and matches the `mechanism_inquiry` prefix surface `\"how is …\"`\n179\tdeclared in `data/seed/meanings-how.lino`; the prompt is read as a mechanism\n180\tquestion about the subject \"it going\". The contracted `\"how's it going?\"` does\n181\tnot match that prefix, routes to `wellbeing` correctly, and is the wording the\n182\tcorpus records.\n183\t\n184\tChanging handler precedence is a behavioral change to the router that this\n185\tissue does not ask for and that would need its own before/after evidence, so\n186\tthe prompt was left out of the corpus rather than the precedence being quietly\n187\treordered. Recorded here so the next person does not rediscover it as a\n188\tmystery.\n189\t\n190\t## 8. Relationship to `tests/unit/multilingual_variations.rs`\n191\t\n192\tThe legacy test is kept as-is. It still asserts what it always asserted, and it\n193\tis not the corpus the floor is measured over — measuring the floor over\n194\thand-written Rust arrays is exactly what left it unenforced for three months.\n195\tThe new corpus is additive: it is data, it is counted, and it is executed.\n196\t"

Counting alone would let a case reach five on\n   wordings the router rejects; this is what stops that.\n\nBoth halves apply the same normalization rule, so they can never disagree about\nhow many wordings a case holds.\n\n**The backfill (R933-3).** Every candidate prompt was first run through the real\nengine (`examples/issue_933_variation_probe.rs`, driven from\n`experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/`) and only the ones that already routed\ncorrectly were recorded; the rest became router work in\n`data/seed/intent-routing.lino` and `data/seed/meanings-intent.lino`, after\nwhich they were re-probed. Final state, printed by the gate on every run:\n\n```text\nConversational wording variations per case (floor: 5 per language)\n  case                  en  ru  hi  zh\n  greeting               9   8   6   7\n  wellbeing              5   6   6   6\n  farewell               8   7   5   5\n  courtesy_response      6   5   5   5\n  identity               6   6   6   6\n  capabilities           6   5   5   5\n  test_status            7   6   5   5\n  assistant_free_time    5   5   5   5\n  assistant_name         5   5   5   5\n  calculation            6   5   5   5\n\nConversational variation floor OK: 10 cases x 4 languages, 228 verified prompts, every group at or above 5.\n```\n\n## 5. Dedup: how this differs from the checks that already existed\n\nThe issue asks for confirmation that this does not overlap\n`check:language-test-coverage`. It does not, and neither do the other two\nlanguage gates:\n\n| Check | Question it answers | Why it cannot catch a four-variation case |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `check:language-test-coverage` | \"Does this pull request's *diff* add test lines mentioning every registered language?\" | Diff-aware: it only fires when a PR touches language-facing files, and it is satisfied by one line per language anywhere in the added tests. A case stuck at four wordings in Hindi trips nothing, forever, as long as nobody edits it. |\n| `check:language-change-parity` | \"Was a change to one language's seed data mirrored into the others?\" | Parity of *edits*, not a count of what exists. Four wordings mirrored across four languages is perfect parity and still below the floor. |\n| `check:intent-coverage` | \"Does every routed intent have a localized response in every advertised language?\" | Counts intents against responses, one per intent per language. It is indifferent to how many prompts reach an intent. |\n| **`check:variation-floor` (new)** | \"Does every conversational test case hold at least five distinct wordings in every advertised language?\" | — |\n\nThe new check is absolute and always-on: it reads the committed corpus, not the\ndiff, so a group that drops below five fails the build on every subsequent run\nuntil it is refilled.\n\n## 6. Verification\n\n| Evidence | What it shows |\n| --- | --- |\n| [`raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt) | The gate passing, with per-language counts printed (R933-7). |\n| [`raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt) | One Hindi `assistant_name` record removed → `- case assistant_name has 4 hi variation(s); the floor is 5`, exit 1 (R933-6, R933-8). |\n| [`raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt) | The same deletion failing the Rust half: `case assistant_name holds 4 hi wording(s); the floor is 5`. |\n| [`raw-data/floor-unit-tests.txt`](raw-data/floor-unit-tests.txt) | 10/10 counting-logic unit tests, including the fixtures engineered to trip the floor (R933-5). |\n| [`raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt`](raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt) | The pre-fix corpus with 8 of 24 groups below the floor. |\n\nReproduce with:\n\n```bash\nnpm run --prefix tests/e2e check:variation-floor\nnode --test tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs\ncargo test --test unit conversational_variation\npython3 experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/legacy-counts.py   # the \"before\" table\n```\n\n## 7. The contracted `\"how's it going?\"` does\nnot match that prefix, routes to `wellbeing` correctly, and is the wording the\ncorpus records.\n\nChanging handler precedence is a behavioral change to the router that this\nissue does not ask for and that would need its own before/after evidence, so\nthe prompt was left out of the corpus rather than the precedence being quietly\nreordered. Recorded here so the next person does not rediscover it as a\nmystery.\n\n## 8. Relationship to `tests/unit/multilingual_variations.rs`\n\nThe legacy test is kept as-is. It still asserts what it always asserted, and it\nis not the corpus the floor is measured over — measuring the floor over\nhand-written Rust arrays is exactly what left it unenforced for three months.\nThe new corpus is additive: it is data, it is counted, and it is executed.\n",

    "originalFile": "# Issue 933 Case Study\n\nIssue [#933](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/933) asks for\nthe CI enforcement that issue\n[#123](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/123) requested and\nPR [#124](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/124) never delivered:\nevery conversational test case must hold **at least five wording variations in\neach of en, ru, hi and zh**, and a check must fail the build when one does not.\n\n## 1. Timeline\n\n- **2026-05-19 08:30** — issue #123 (*\"Unknown prompt: Купи слона\"*) is filed.\n- **2026-05-19 08:34** — konard comments\n  ([#123 comment](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/123#issuecomment-4485896648)):\n  *\"All features should be supported in all 4 languages with multiple\n  variations in wording, we should not stop until each test will have at least\n  5 variations per 4 languages, also I think we should have CI/CD checks to\n  enforce that for all the test cases.\"*\n- **2026-05-19 09:50** — PR #124 (*\"Fix reported browser prompt examples\"*)\n  merges. It fixes the reported prompts. No counting check ships with it.\n- **2026-08-04** — issue #933 separates the missing enforcement into its own\n  task.\n- **2026-08-14** — PR [#1010](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1010)\n  delivers it. The issue body, verbatim, is in\n  [`raw-data/issue-933.md`](raw-data/issue-933.md).\n\n## 2. Requirement matrix\n\n| ID | Requirement (issue #933) | Delivered as |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R933-1 | Define a machine-checkable convention for \"wording variation\". | A manifest, `data/benchmarks/conversational-variations-suite.lino`, listing the cases, the languages, the floor and the per-language partition files; one record per prompt in `data/benchmarks/conversational-variations/<language>.lino`. Two prompts count as one wording unless they differ in more than case, punctuation, symbols or spacing. |\n| R933-2 | A CI script in the style of `check-language-parity` that walks the corpus and fails below five in any of en/ru/hi/zh. | `tests/e2e/scripts/check-conversational-variation-floor.mjs`, run as `npm run --prefix tests/e2e check:variation-floor`. |\n| R933-3 | Backfill variations until the check passes. | 228 prompts across 10 cases × 4 languages, every group at or above five; the router phrasings they needed were added to `data/seed/intent-routing.lino` and `data/seed/meanings-intent.lino`. |\n| R933-4 | Wire the check into `release.yml`. | `data/meta/ci-gates/check-conversational-variation-floor.lino`, stage `web`. Since issue #991 the workflow no longer holds a step list: `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs `rust-script scripts/run-ci-gates.rs --stage web`, which loads this shard. |\n| R933-5 | Automated: the CI script itself, plus a unit test on its counting logic using fixture data engineered to trip the floor. | `tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs` — 10 cases feeding `auditVariationFloor` fixtures at 4/5, at 0, and at five re-punctuated copies of one phrase. |\n| R933-6 | Manual: reduce one test case to 4 variations in one language and confirm local failure. | [`raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt) and [`raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt). |\n| R933-7 | Multilingual: confirm coverage counts print per language. | The count table prints on success as well as failure — [`raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt). |\n| R933-8 | Verbose output listing exactly which test cases are under the floor. | One `- case <name> has <n> <language> variation(s); the floor is 5` line per shortfall, plus a remediation line naming the file to edit. |\n| R933-9 | Standing clauses: `docs/case-studies/issue-933/`, single PR. | This document; PR #1010. |\n| R933-10 | Dedup: confirm no overlap with `check:language-test-coverage` and note it here. | Section 5. |\n\n## 3. Root cause: nothing counted anything\n\nThe conversational corpus was `tests/unit/multilingual_variations.rs` — hand-written\nprompt arrays with a comment stating the intended count (*\"Farewells — 8-9\nvariants per language\"*). Comments are not checks, and a hand-written array has\nno notion of how many distinct wordings it holds, so the corpus drifted below\nthe floor without anything noticing. Measured with the same normalization the\nnew check applies, **8 of its 24 case × language groups sat below five**\n([`raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt`](raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt)):\n\n```text\n  case                  en  ru  hi  zh\n  assistant_free_time    6   4   3   3\n  calculation           16   8  10  11\n  farewell               5   2   5   5\n  greeting               6   4   5   6\n  identity              11   7   6   6\n  wellbeing              5   3   3   3\n```\n\n`farewell`/`ru` is the clearest case. The array holds five Russian entries —\n`\"пока\"`, `\"пока!\"`, `\"Пока.\"`, `\"до свидания\"`, `\"досвидания\"` — which look\nlike five variations and are two: one word re-punctuated three times, and one\nphrase re-spaced twice. Counting array elements would have called that group\nfull. This is why the floor is defined over *normalized* prompts, and why the\nunit test *\"re-punctuated copies of one wording do not add up to five\"* exists.\n\n## 4. What was built\n\n**The convention (R933-1).** A benchmark corpus, following the issue #819\nprecedent (`data/benchmarks/local-path-discovery-suite.lino` plus per-language\npartitions plus a corpus-driven Rust runner). The manifest declares the floor\nitself, so the number is data:\n\n```text\nconversational_variation_suite_issue_933\n  record_type \"conversational_variation_suite\"\n  minimum_variations_per_language \"5\"\n  languages \"en|ru|hi|zh\"\n  case \"greeting\"\n  ...\n```\n\nEach record is a prompt with the intent and evidence link it must produce:\n\n```text\nconversational_variation_case_greeting_hi_01\n  record_type \"conversational_variation_case\"\n  id \"greeting_hi_01\"\n  case \"greeting\"\n  language \"hi\"\n  source \"self_authored_multilingual_variation\"\n  prompt \"नमस्ते\"\n  expected_intent \"greeting\"\n  expected_evidence \"response:greeting\"\n```\n\n**The gate has two halves, and both are needed.**\n\n1. `tests/e2e/scripts/check-conversational-variation-floor.mjs` counts. It also\n   rejects the ways a group could look full without being full: a duplicate id,\n   a record whose case or language the manifest does not list, a partition file\n   holding another language's records, a prompt that is empty once punctuation\n   is stripped, and a prompt that only re-punctuates one already counted.\n2. `tests/unit/conversational_variations.rs` answers every recorded prompt with\n   `FormalAiEngine` and asserts the routed intent, the evidence link and — for\n   arithmetic — the answer text. Counting alone would let a case reach five on\n   wordings the router rejects; this is what stops that.\n\nBoth halves apply the same normalization rule, so they can never disagree about\nhow many wordings a case holds.\n\n**The backfill (R933-3).** Every candidate prompt was first run through the real\nengine (`examples/issue_933_variation_probe.rs`, driven from\n`experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/`) and only the ones that already routed\ncorrectly were recorded; the rest became router work in\n`data/seed/intent-routing.lino` and `data/seed/meanings-intent.lino`, after\nwhich they were re-probed. Final state, printed by the gate on every run:\n\n```text\nConversational wording variations per case (floor: 5 per language)\n  case                  en  ru  hi  zh\n  greeting               9   8   6   7\n  wellbeing              5   6   6   6\n  farewell               8   7   5   5\n  courtesy_response      6   5   5   5\n  identity               6   6   6   6\n  capabilities           6   5   5   5\n  test_status            7   6   5   5\n  assistant_free_time    5   5   5   5\n  assistant_name         5   5   5   5\n  calculation            6   5   5   5\n\nConversational variation floor OK: 10 cases x 4 languages, 228 verified prompts, every group at or above 5.\n```\n\n## 5. Dedup: how this differs from the checks that already existed\n\nThe issue asks for confirmation that this does not overlap\n`check:language-test-coverage`. It does not, and neither do the other two\nlanguage gates:\n\n| Check | Question it answers | Why it cannot catch a four-variation case |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `check:language-test-coverage` | \"Does this pull request's *diff* add test lines mentioning every registered language?\" | Diff-aware: it only fires when a PR touches language-facing files, and it is satisfied by one line per language anywhere in the added tests. A case stuck at four wordings in Hindi trips nothing, forever, as long as nobody edits it. |\n| `check:language-change-parity` | \"Was a change to one language's seed data mirrored into the others?\" | Parity of *edits*, not a count of what exists. Four wordings mirrored across four languages is perfect parity and still below the floor. |\n| `check:intent-coverage` | \"Does every routed intent have a localized response in every advertised language?\" | Counts intents against responses, one per intent per language. It is indifferent to how many prompts reach an intent. |\n| **`check:variation-floor` (new)** | \"Does every conversational test case hold at least five distinct wordings in every advertised language?\" | — |\n\nThe new check is absolute and always-on: it reads the committed corpus, not the\ndiff, so a group that drops below five fails the build on every subsequent run\nuntil it is refilled.\n\n## 6. Verification\n\n| Evidence | What it shows |\n| --- | --- |\n| [`raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt) | The gate passing, with per-language counts printed (R933-7). |\n| [`raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt) | One Hindi `assistant_name` record removed → `- case assistant_name has 4 hi variation(s); the floor is 5`, exit 1 (R933-6, R933-8). |\n| [`raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt) | The same deletion failing the Rust half: `case assistant_name holds 4 hi wording(s); the floor is 5`. |\n| [`raw-data/floor-unit-tests.txt`](raw-data/floor-unit-tests.txt) | 10/10 counting-logic unit tests, including the fixtures engineered to trip the floor (R933-5). |\n| [`raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt`](raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt) | The pre-fix corpus with 8 of 24 groups below the floor. |\n\nReproduce with:\n\n```bash\nnpm run --prefix tests/e2e check:variation-floor\nnode --test tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs\ncargo test --test unit conversational_variation\npython3 experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/legacy-counts.py   # the \"before\" table\n```\n\n## 7. Defect found while backfilling, and not fixed here\n\n`\"how is it going?\"` does not reach the `wellbeing` intent. It is intercepted\nearlier by `try_how_it_works` (`src/solver_handler_how.rs`), which runs before\nintent routing and matches the `mechanism_inquiry` prefix surface `\"how is …\"`\ndeclared in `data/seed/meanings-how.lino`; the prompt is read as a mechanism\nquestion about the subject \"it going\". The contracted `\"how's it going?\"` does\nnot match that prefix, routes to `wellbeing` correctly, and is the wording the\ncorpus records.\n\nChanging handler precedence is a behavioral change to the router that this\nissue does not ask for and that would need its own before/after evidence, so\nthe prompt was left out of the corpus rather than the precedence being quietly\nreordered. Recorded here so the next person does not rediscover it as a\nmystery.\n\n## 8. Relationship to `tests/unit/multilingual_variations.rs`\n\nThe legacy test is kept as-is. It still asserts what it always asserted, and it\nis not the corpus the floor is measured over — measuring the floor over\nhand-written Rust arrays is exactly what left it unenforced for three months.\nThe new corpus is additive: it is data, it is counted, and it is executed.\n",

    "originalFile": "# Issue 933 Case Study\n\nIssue [#933](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/933) asks for\nthe CI enforcement that issue\n[#123](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/123) requested and\nPR [#124](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/124) never delivered:\nevery conversational test case must hold **at least five wording variations in\neach of en, ru, hi and zh**, and a check must fail the build when one does not.\n\n## 1. Timeline\n\n- **2026-05-19 08:30** — issue #123 (*\"Unknown prompt: Купи слона\"*) is filed.\n- **2026-05-19 08:34** — konard comments\n  ([#123 comment](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/123#issuecomment-4485896648)):\n  *\"All features should be supported in all 4 languages with multiple\n  variations in wording, we should not stop until each test will have at least\n  5 variations per 4 languages, also I think we should have CI/CD checks to\n  enforce that for all the test cases.\"*\n- **2026-05-19 09:50** — PR #124 (*\"Fix reported browser prompt examples\"*)\n  merges. It fixes the reported prompts. No counting check ships with it.\n- **2026-08-04** — issue #933 separates the missing enforcement into its own\n  task.\n- **2026-08-14** — PR [#1010](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1010)\n  delivers it. The issue body, verbatim, is in\n  [`raw-data/issue-933.md`](raw-data/issue-933.md).\n\n## 2. Requirement matrix\n\n| ID | Requirement (issue #933) | Delivered as |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R933-1 | Define a machine-checkable convention for \"wording variation\". | A manifest, `data/benchmarks/conversational-variations-suite.lino`, listing the cases, the languages, the floor and the per-language partition files; one record per prompt in `data/benchmarks/conversational-variations/<language>.lino`. Two prompts count as one wording unless they differ in more than case, punctuation, symbols or spacing. |\n| R933-2 | A CI script in the style of `check-language-parity` that walks the corpus and fails below five in any of en/ru/hi/zh. | `tests/e2e/scripts/check-conversational-variation-floor.mjs`, run as `npm run --prefix tests/e2e check:variation-floor`. |\n| R933-3 | Backfill variations until the check passes. | 228 prompts across 10 cases × 4 languages, every group at or above five; the router phrasings they needed were added to `data/seed/intent-routing.lino` and `data/seed/meanings-intent.lino`. |\n| R933-4 | Wire the check into `release.yml`. | `data/meta/ci-gates/check-conversational-variation-floor.lino`, stage `web`. Since issue #991 the workflow no longer holds a step list: `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs `rust-script scripts/run-ci-gates.rs --stage web`, which loads this shard. |\n| R933-5 | Automated: the CI script itself, plus a unit test on its counting logic using fixture data engineered to trip the floor. | `tests/web/conversational-variation-floor.test.mjs` — 10 cases feeding `auditVariationFloor` fixtures at 4/5, at 0, and at five re-punctuated copies of one phrase. |\n| R933-6 | Manual: reduce one test case to 4 variations in one language and confirm local failure. | [`raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-manual-failure.txt) and [`raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt`](raw-data/rust-corpus-manual-failure.txt). |\n| R933-7 | Multilingual: confirm coverage counts print per language. | The count table prints on success as well as failure — [`raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt`](raw-data/floor-check-pass.txt). |\n| R933-8 | Verbose output listing exactly which test cases are under the floor. | One `- case <name> has <n> <language> variation(s); the floor is 5` line per shortfall, plus a remediation line naming the file to edit. |\n| R933-9 | Standing clauses: `docs/case-studies/issue-933/`, single PR. | This document; PR #1010. |\n| R933-10 | Dedup: confirm no overlap with `check:language-test-coverage` and note it here. | Section 5. |\n\n## 3. Root cause: nothing counted anything\n\nThe conversational corpus was `tests/unit/multilingual_variations.rs` — hand-written\nprompt arrays with a comment stating the intended count (*\"Farewells — 8-9\nvariants per language\"*). Comments are not checks, and a hand-written array has\nno notion of how many distinct wordings it holds, so the corpus drifted below\nthe floor without anything noticing. Measured with the same normalization the\nnew check applies, **8 of its 24 case × language groups sat below five**\n([`raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt`](raw-data/legacy-counts-before.txt)):\n\n```text\n  case                  en  ru  hi  zh\n  assistant_free_time    6   4   3   3\n  calculation           16   8  10  11\n  farewell               5   2   5   5\n  greeting               6   4   5   6\n  identity              11   7   6   6\n  wellbeing              5   3   3   3\n```\n\n`farewell`/`ru` is the clearest case. The array holds five Russian entries —\n`\"пока\"`, `\"пока!\"`, `\"Пока.\"`, `\"до свидания\"`, `\"досвидания\"` — which look\nlike five variations and are two: one word re-punctuated three times, and one\nphrase re-spaced twice. Counting array elements would have called that group\nfull. This is why the floor is defined over *normalized* prompts, and why the\nunit test *\"re-punctuated copies of one wording do not add up to five\"* exists.\n\n## 4. What was built\n\n**The convention (R933-1).** A benchmark corpus, following the issue #819\nprecedent (`data/benchmarks/local-path-discovery-suite.lino` plus per-language\npartitions plus a corpus-driven Rust runner). The manifest declares the floor\nitself, so the number is data:\n\n```text\nconversational_variation_suite_issue_933\n  record_type \"conversational_variation_suite\"\n  minimum_variations_per_language \"5\"\n  languages \"en|ru|hi|zh\"\n  case \"greeting\"\n  ...\n```\n\nEach record is a prompt with the intent, the evidence link and the answer it\nmust produce:\n\n```text\nconversational_variation_case_greeting_hi_01\n  record_type \"conversational_variation_case\"\n  id \"greeting_hi_01\"\n  case \"greeting\"\n  language \"hi\"\n  source \"self_authored_multilingual_variation\"\n  prompt \"नमस्ते\"\n  expected_intent \"greeting\"\n  expected_evidence \"response:greeting\"\n  expected_answer \"नमस्ते, मैं आपकी कैसे मदद कर सकता हूँ?\"\n```\n\n`expected_answer` is what makes the corpus documentation rather than a table of\ncounts: a reader sees the exact text each of the 228 wordings produces, which is\nthe rule `scripts/check-tests-as-docs.rs` enforces for behavioural tests\n(R234-2). The multi-paragraph capability listing is recorded by its opening line\nwith `expected_answer_contains` instead of being inlined 21 times, and the\narithmetic records add the computed value the same way. A record carrying\nneither field is rejected by the floor gate, so the next case cannot be added\nwithout showing what it answers.\n\n**The gate has two halves, and both are needed.**\n\n1. `tests/e2e/scripts/check-conversational-variation-floor.mjs` counts. It also\n   rejects the ways a group could look full without being full: a duplicate id,\n   a record whose case or language the manifest does not list, a partition file\n   holding another language's records, a prompt that is empty once punctuation\n   is stripped, and a prompt that only re-punctuates one already counted.\n2. `tests/unit/conversational_variations.rs` answers every recorded prompt with\n   `FormalAiEngine` and asserts the routed intent, the evidence link and — for\n   arithmetic — the answer text. Counting alone would let a case reach five on\n   wordings the router rejects; this is what stops that.\n\nBoth halves apply the same normalization rule, so they can never disagree about\nhow many wordings a case holds.\n\n**The backfill (R933-3).** Every candidate prompt was first run through the real\nengine (`examples/issue_933_variation_probe.rs`, driven from\n`experiments/issue_933_variation_floor/`) and only the ones that already routed\ncorrectly were recorded; the rest became router work in\n`data/seed/intent-routing.lino` and `data/seed/meanings-intent.lino`, after\nwhich they were re-probed. Final state, printed by the gate on every run:\n\n```text\nConversational wording variations per case (floor: 5 per language)\n  case                  en  ru  hi  zh\n  greeting               9   8   6   7\n  wellbeing              5   6   6   6\n  farewell               8   7   5   5\n  courtesy_response      6   5   5   5\n  identity               6   6   6   6\n  capabilities           6   5   5   5\n  test_status            7   6   5   5\n  assistant_free_time    5   5   5   5\n  assistant_name         5   5   5   5\n  calculation            6   5   5   5\n\nConversational variation floor OK: 10 cases x 4 languages, 228 verified prompts, every group at or above 5.\n```\n\n## 5. Dedup: how this differs from the checks that already existed\n\nThe issue asks for confirmation that this does not overlap\n`check:language-test-coverage`. It does not, and neither do the other two\nlanguage gates:\n\n| Check | Question it answers | Why it cannot catch a four-variation case |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `check:language-test-coverage` | \"Does this pull request's *diff* add test lines mentioning every registered language?\" | Diff-aware: it only fires when a PR touches language-facing files, and it is satisfied by one line per language anywhere in the added tests. A case stuck at four wordings in Hindi trips nothing, forever, as long as nobody edits it. |\n| `check:language-change-parity` | \"Was a change to one language's seed data mirrored into the others?\" | Parity of *edits*, not a count of what exists. Four wordings mirrored across four languages is perfect parity and still below the floor. |\n| `check:intent-coverage` | \"Does every routed intent have a localized response in every advertised language?\" | Counts intents against responses, one per intent per language. It is indifferent to how many prompts reach an intent. |\n| **`check:variation-floor` (new)** | \"Does every conversational test case hold at least five distinct wordings in every advertised language?\" | — |\n\nThe new check is absolute and always-on: it reads the committed corpus, not the\ndiff, so a group that drops below five fails the build on every subsequent run\nuntil it is refilled.\n\n## 6.
